input.prompt:
Investigating a Sentry App Hang crash (WORKROOM-2Y) in a macOS SwiftUI app (repo at /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom, app code under macapp/). Stack trace shows the hang happens inside AppDelegate.applicationWillFinishLaunching / AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching, with in-app frames leading into Combine's `Publishers.Filter.Inner`, then into Swift runtime generic metadata resolution (`_swift_getGenericMetadata`, `swift_getTypeByMangledName`, `DecodedMetadataBuilder::createBoundGenericType`). This pattern (slow first-use generic metadata demangling for a Combine operator chain) strongly suggests a `.filter` operator on some Combine publisher (NotificationCenter.publisher, @Published property, custom Publisher, etc.) that is being subscribed to synchronously during app launch (applicationWillFinishLaunching or applicationDidFinishLaunching), and the FIRST TIME that generic Publishers.Filter<...> specialization is instantiated it triggers a slow runtime type-metadata lookup (dyld/Swift demangler), causing the app to hang the main thread for 2+ seconds at launch.

Please find and report back:
1. The file and exact contents of AppDelegate.swift (or whatever file defines applicationWillFinishLaunching / applicationDidFinishLaunching) — path and line numbers.
2. Every place in macapp/ where `.filter(` is chained on a Combine publisher (grep for `.filter` near `.sink`, `.receive`, `Publishers`, `@Published`, `NotificationCenter.default.publisher`, `AnyPublisher`, etc.) — especially any such chains that are set up eagerly inside AppDelegate's launch methods, or in singletons/services that AppDelegate initializes during launch (e.g. WindowRegistry, any AppState/AppDelegate-owned observers, menu bar setup, etc.).
3. Any code that runs at launch time (applicationWillFinishLaunching/applicationDidFinishLaunching or things called synchronously from them, including init of AppDelegate's stored properties) that sets up Combine subscriptions, especially chains combining multiple generic operators (`.filter`, `.map`, `.compactMap`, `.combineLatest`, `.debounce`) since these compound generic types are the ones most likely to trigger slow metadata specialization the first time they're used.
4. Whether there's an existing pattern in the codebase of deferring Combine subscription setup to avoid startup cost (e.g. DispatchQueue.main.async wrapping, lazy properties, or comments referencing "AppHang" or "dyld" or "_dyld_find_foreign_type_protocol_conformance" — there's a known prior incident in this codebase about a toolbar item's SwiftUI `.toolbar` causing a similar dyld-metadata-scan App Hang, fixed by using a plain empty AppKit NSToolbar instead of SwiftUI toolbar modifiers; check if there's a similar precedent of code being restructured to avoid Swift runtime metadata scanning at hot paths).

Report exact file paths, line numbers, and relevant code snippets for each of the above. Keep the report focused and factual — do not propose fixes, just report what you find.

## 1. AppDelegate.swift / launch methods

The AppDelegate lives inside `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/WorkroomApp.swift` (no separate `AppDelegate.swift` file). There is **no** `applicationWillFinishLaunching` implementation anywhere in `macapp/` (grep found none). Only `applicationDidFinishLaunching` exists, at:

- `WorkroomApp.swift:250-496` — `func applicationDidFinishLaunching(_ notification: Notification)`
- Class declared at `WorkroomApp.swift:169`: `final class AppDelegate: NSObject, NSApplicationDelegate, UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate`

Relevant synchronous work inside it, in order:
- `WorkroomApp.swift:256` `NSWindow.allowsAutomaticWindowTabbing = false`
- `WorkroomApp.swift:259` `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate = self`
- `WorkroomApp.swift:263` `menuBarController = MenuBarController(registry: .shared)` — **eagerly constructs a Combine subscription** (see §2/§3 below)
- `WorkroomApp.swift:268-269` `SwitcherPanelController.shared.prepare()` / `.attach(to: .shared)` — pre-builds an `NSHostingView`/`NSPanel` (no Combine)
- `WorkroomApp.swift:275-279` `NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: .willResignActiveNotification, ...)` — plain block-based observer, not Combine
- `WorkroomApp.swift:281-471` installs an `NSEvent` local key monitor (large switch of shortcut handling, no Combine)
- `WorkroomApp.swift:480-485` `updateGlobalHotkey()` + `hotkeyObservation = Task { for await _ in Defaults.updates(...) }` — async-sequence based, not Combine
- `WorkroomApp.swift:489-493` another plain `NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: .showQuickTerminal, ...)`
- `WorkroomApp.swift:495` `installSigtermHandler()`

Also relevant, run just before the Scene body (i.e., effectively at launch, ahead of `applicationDidFinishLaunching`), inside `WorkroomApp.init()` (`WorkroomApp.swift:17-53`):
- `WorkroomApp.swift:21` `SentryConfig.start()`
- `WorkroomApp.swift:33` `setenv("PATH", ...)`
- `@StateObject private var updater = Updater()` (`WorkroomApp.swift:11`) — constructs a Combine chain in `Updater.init` (see §2)
- `@StateObject private var whatsNew = WhatsNewService(...)` (`WorkroomApp.swift:15`) — no Combine, pure array filtering only

## 2. Every `.filter(` chained on a Combine publisher in macapp/

**None found.** I grepped exhaustively for `.filter(`, `.filter {` (trailing closure form), and `Publishers.` across all of `macapp/` (excluding `build/`/`DerivedData/`), plus every file that `import Combine`. Every single `.filter` hit in the codebase is a plain `Array`/`Sequence`/`String`/`Set` filter (e.g. `AppStore.swift:695`, `WindowRegistry.swift:107,169,239`, `QuickSwitcher.swift:187`, `WhatsNewService.swift:97,105`, `ProjectStore.swift:184`, `NotificationCenterStore.swift`, `VCSWriting.swift`, `AgentSessionIndex.swift`, `FileTree.swift`, `PickerModel.swift`, `CommitDraft.swift`, `SwitcherRailView.swift:52`, `ThemeService.swift:172`, etc.). None of them follow a `.publisher`, `$property`, `NotificationCenter.default.publisher`, or `.sink`/`.receive` chain — no `Publishers.Filter<...>` specialization exists anywhere in this app's source.

`import Combine` appears in exactly six files:
`MenuBarController.swift`, `Updater.swift`, `FileFind.swift`, `FileTreeModel.swift`, `AppStore.swift`, `TerminalSearch.swift` — none of them use `.filter` on a publisher.

## 3. Combine subscriptions that DO run at launch time

Two genuine Combine chains are wired up synchronously during launch — both compound-generic operator chains, neither containing `.filter`, but matching the "first-use generic metadata specialization" hazard described:

**a) `MenuBarController.init`** — `WorkroomApp/Core/MenuBarController.swift:49-52`, constructed directly from `AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching` at `WorkroomApp.swift:263`:
```swift
registry.$aggregateUnread
  .receive(on: RunLoop.main)
  .sink { [weak self] total in self?.applyCount(total) }
  .store(in: &cancellables)
```
This is `Published<Int>.Publisher` → `Publishers.ReceiveOn<...>` → `.sink`, instantiated for the first time ever at exactly this call site during `applicationDidFinishLaunching`.

**b) `Updater.init`** — `WorkroomApp/Core/Updater.swift:32-33`, constructed via `@StateObject private var updater = Updater()` at `WorkroomApp.swift:11` (runs as part of `WorkroomApp` struct's stored-property init, ahead of/alongside `WorkroomApp.init()`'s body and the Scene, i.e., on the app-launch path):
```swift
controller.updater.publisher(for: \.canCheckForUpdates)
  .assign(to: &$canCheckForUpdates)
```
This is an `NSObject.KeyValueObservingPublisher<SPUUpdater, Bool>` → `.assign(to:)` into a `@Published` projected value — another compound generic Combine chain, first instantiated here at launch.

Both are candidates for the "first-use generic metadata specialization" hang pattern the Sentry stack trace describes, even though neither uses `.filter` specifically — the ticket's premise of a `.filter` operator being the exact culprit doesn't match anything actually present in the codebase.

## 4. Prior precedent of restructuring to avoid Swift-runtime/dyld metadata scanning at hot paths

There is a well-documented, closely analogous **prior incident** in this exact codebase — not about Combine, but about SwiftUI's `.toolbar` modifier triggering the same class of dyld/runtime-metadata-scan hang, exactly as referenced in the task:

- `WorkroomApp/Core/WindowBackgroundThemer.swift:49-63` — comment explains that `NavigationSplitView` auto-injects a SwiftUI-owned toolbar sidebar-toggle item, which keeps `AppKitToolbarItem.updateMenuFormRepresentation` alive; that method "bridges an NSAttributedString attributes dict into `swift_dynamicCast` → `_dyld_find_foreign_type_protocol_conformance` (a linear scan of every loaded Mach-O image ... stacking up to the ≥2s macOS-26 AppHangs)." Fix: `window.toolbar?.isVisible = false` set directly via AppKit (not `.toolbar(removing:)`, which is a no-op since SwiftUI still owns/re-injects it).
- Same fix re-applied/re-asserted in `AppStore.swift:1044-1057` (`attachWindow`) and referenced again in `WorkroomApp.swift:65-70` and `RootView.swift:395`.
- `WorkroomApp.swift:78-81` also documents the menu-bar item itself being hand-managed via `MenuBarController`/`NSStatusItem` rather than SwiftUI's `MenuBarExtra`, for unrelated behavioral reasons (not performance), but it's part of the same "avoid letting SwiftUI own AppKit surfaces at hot/frequent paths" pattern.

Other prior App Hang incidents tracked in this codebase (same Sentry project, different mechanisms — not Combine/dyld-metadata, but useful pattern context):
- **WORKROOM-2B** — a ≥2000ms App Hang from over-invalidating SwiftUI rows on every terminal-title/activity-pulse publish; fixed via careful `@Published` dependency scoping (see `HistoryPanel.swift`, `ChangesPanel.swift`, `AppStore.swift:4055`, `FocusedTabSelection.swift`, `SwitcherRailView.swift:9`, `UITestFixture.swift:213`, and `SentryConfig.swift:61` — this is also where the nightly/production Sentry-environment split originated).
- **WORKROOM-2S** — an AppHang from AttributeGraph deep-comparing a large array (`sbsRows`) on every file switch in `DiffViewer.swift`; fixed by boxing it into a reference type (`DiffViewer.swift:70,457`, `DiffViewerSideBySideRowsTests.swift`).
- **WORKROOM-2T** — an AppHang from eager `List`/`ScrollView` row materialization on large diffs; fixed by switching to lazy `List` rendering (`DiffViewer.swift:385-396,424,547`, `DiffViewerLazyRenderingTests.swift`).

I found **no existing reference to WORKROOM-2Y** anywhere in the codebase (it hasn't been triaged/fixed yet), and **no existing pattern of deferring Combine subscription setup** specifically (no `DispatchQueue.main.async` wrapping a `.sink`/`.filter` chain, no lazy-Combine-property pattern, no comment mentioning "AppHang" + "Combine"/"metadata"/"demangl" together). The only deferred-setup pattern in the launch path is unrelated to Combine: `WindowBackgroundThemer.swift:15` wraps its `NSWindow` lookup in `DispatchQueue.main.async`, and `WorkroomApp.swift:44-46` defers `ShellEnvironment.refresh()` via `Task.detached`.</result>
